corrections.original: SuperVision submitted its results on 30 September 2012
corrections.fix: 30 Sep 2012 (Sunday, 23:00 GMT) was the deadline, extended on 17 Sep; SuperVision's own submission day is not published. Say 'by the 30 September deadline'.

corrections.original: Paper's '150,000 testing images' is looser phrasing than ILSVRC-2012's ~100,000
corrections.fix: The paper's 1.2M/50K/150K describes ILSVRC (2010 split); ILSVRC-2012 had 100,000 test images (150,000 val+test minus 50,000 val; Karpathy: 'full test set of 100,000 images').

corrections.original: 224 input only works as 227; most reimplementations use 227; cause UNVERIFIED; Wikipedia credits Karpathy
corrections.fix: Original 2012 code computes conv output as 1+ceil((2p+n-f)/s), so 224 with padding=0 gives 55: the paper is internally consistent under cuda-convnet's convention. Caffe uses 227 but torchvision uses 224 with padding=2, so 'most use 227' is overstated. Current Wikipedia has no Karpathy attribution; removed.

corrections.original: Zeiler & Fergus replicated AlexNet single-model result to within 0.2%
corrections.fix: Paper says 'within 0.1% of their reported value on the ImageNet 2012 validation set'.

corrections.original: By ILSVRC 2013 the entire top five classification entries were convnets
corrections.fix: All top-five teams used CNNs, but NUS (2nd, 0.12953) was a hybrid: rectified CNN outputs combined with its refined PASCAL VOC12 winning (traditional) solution.

corrections.original: Jitendra Malik: late 50s in 2012
corrections.fix: Born 11 Oct 1960, so 51-52 in 2012: early 50s.

corrections.original: Fei-Fei Li: late 30s in 2012
corrections.fix: Born 3 Jul 1976, so 36 in 2012.

corrections.original: Krizhevsky born in the Ukrainian SSR, per Wikipedia (VERIFIED-SECONDARY)
corrections.fix: Current Wikipedia states no birthplace or birth year ('Year of birth missing'); no reliable source found. Do not state.

corrections.original: Karpathy 2 Sep 2014: 'Human accuracy is not a point...' and the ~3% expert-ensemble estimate
corrections.fix: Both come from the post's February 2015 update, not the 2 Sep 2014 original. Other labellers: one expert ~12% on 280 images; labmates with pruned interface 13-15%.

corrections.original: VGG on LRN (from-memory quote: 'does not improve on the model A without any normalisation layers')
corrections.fix: Verified text: 'such normalisation does not improve the performance on the ILSVRC dataset, but leads to increased memory consumption and computation time'; A-LRN 29.7/10.5 vs A 29.6/10.4.

corrections.original: Batch Normalization ~4.8-4.9% top-5, exceeding human raters (from memory)
corrections.fix: Verified: '4.9% top-5 validation error (and 4.8% test error), exceeding the accuracy of human raters' (4.82% per ILSVRC server); arXiv 11 Feb 2015.

corrections.original: GTX 580 reached market 'late 2010' (month from memory)
corrections.fix: Launched 9 November 2010 as the first GeForce 500-series card.

corrections.original: NIPS 2012 3-8 Dec at Harrah's/Harveys (dates from memory)
corrections.fix: Verified: 'Mon Dec 3rd through Sat the 8th, Harrahs and Harveys, Lake Tahoe'. Status upgraded.

corrections.original: Auction: DeepMind dropped out early, then Microsoft; laptop on an upturned wastebasket; Wired page not fetched
corrections.fix: Wired (16 Mar 2021) read directly: DeepMind bid in shares and dropped out; Microsoft dropped out at $15-20M, returned, dropped out again near $22M; window cut to 30 min; laptop 'sat on a trash can turned upside down on a table'; the Google dinner was on Hinton's 65th birthday; stopped at $44M, chose Google.

corrections.original: ISI (runner-up, 0.26172) used Fisher Vectors + Graphical Gaussian Vectors
corrections.fix: The scoring entry is described as weighted sum of SIFT+FV, LBP+FV, GIST+FV, CSIFT+FV classifiers; GGV appears only in the team abstract. Say 'Fisher Vectors'.

corrections.original: Two-GPU split cut error 1.7%/1.2% vs a half-size one-GPU net
corrections.fix: Paper's footnote 2: the one-GPU baseline kept full size in the last conv and FC layers, so the comparison 'is biased in favor of the one-GPU net' (it was bigger than half).

corrections.original: Hinton could not travel because of his back
corrections.fix: Li: 'Hinton couldn't attend because of a chronic back problem'. He could not sit (so no flights) but travelled overland to Lake Tahoe lying down in December 2012. Say 'did not attend because of his back'.

corrections.original: Sutskever GTC 2023 'great fit for GPUs ... unbelievably fast' wording comes from a summary (UNVERIFIED)
corrections.fix: NVIDIA's blog prints it in quotation marks as Sutskever's words, in two fragments joined by blog prose: VERIFIED-SECONDARY as fragments; check the video before quoting as one sentence.

corrections.original: Jensen Huang (GTC 2023) said AlexNet trained on '14 million images' and 'ignited the big bang of AI' [S48]
corrections.fix: S48 contains no '14 million'; 'Big Bang of AI' is the blog author's paraphrase, not a quote. Attribution unverified; the number is wrong regardless.

corrections.original: LeCun: 'an unequivocal turning point in the history of computer vision'
corrections.fix: Trail now leads to Cade Metz (Genius Makers), relayed by Timothy B. Lee ('This is proof.'); no primary record and Metz page unread. Use the CHM's paraphrase 'pronounced it a turning point for AI', or attribute to Metz.

corrections.original: Training ran in Krizhevsky's bedroom at his parents' house
corrections.fix: CHM (with Krizhevsky's clarifications, Hinton's review) says bedroom; NVIDIA's 2023 blog says 'a few GeForce GTX 580 GPUs in a University of Toronto lab'. Prefer CHM; note conflict.

corrections.original: ILSVRC 2012 workshop discussion until 18:00
corrections.fix: ILSVRC page says 17:30-18:00 discussion; PASCAL VOC page lists the ILSVRC block 15:30-18:15. Malik gave an invited PASCAL talk 14:30-15:00 the same day.

corrections.original: Hinton Toronto Star quote 'work on whatever we like...' (via Varsity)
corrections.fix: Re-verified via Wayback copy (live page 403); extended with the following sentence 'It doesn't put any constraints on what we work on and when we publish'.

corrections.original: LeCun 2012 CVPR open letter 'So, I'm giving up on submitting to computer vision conferences altogether.'
corrections.fix: No primary text retrieved; remains UNVERIFIED.

corrections.original: LeCun: 'In 2012, you couldn't get a paper accepted at CVPR if you used neural networks...'
corrections.fix: No source; remains UNVERIFIED.

corrections.original: Hinton's '1% improvement buys a week' anecdote with Krizhevsky
corrections.fix: Only divergent second-hand retellings; remains UNVERIFIED.

corrections.original: Sutskever Eye on AI podcast line
corrections.fix: Transcript not retrieved; remains UNVERIFIED.
